In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and characterization of a series of cyclophane-anchored diruthenium compounds with two electroactive vinyl ruthenium moietes, and their use for the investigation of electronic communication between these moieties.
the synthesis of a series of novel cyclophane- and cyclophane-like complexes, which are based on a cyclophane backbone with a central metal atom.
the synthesis, structure, and electronic properties of a series of new vinyl ruthenium complexes with a cyclophane scaffold.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “through-space” pathway is the dominating factor in the electron delocalization between the two electroactive vinyl ruthenium moities in these complexes.
the “closed” [2.2]-paracyclophanes are the best candidates for the realization of a “molecular wire” in the class of the vinyl ruthenium cyclophanes.
the “through-space” pathway is the more effective one in the case of the “closed” cyclophane 2, while both pathways are of similar efficiency for the “half-closed” cyclophanes 1 and 3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electronic coupling in radical cations of these cyclophane-bridge diruthenium systems is dominated by the through-space pathway.
electron delocalization in these complexes is not limited to the vinyl ruthenium moities, as it is in the monoruthene complex 1, but extends to the whole cyclophane scaffold.
the through-space pathway is not only operative for the radical cation but also in the ground-state of the mixed-valent complex.
